new_packages.label_en: Netzach and Hod — The Feet and the Lips

bechina_evidence.translation: The feet are an aspect of Netzach and Hod
Through the lips, which are Netzach and Hod

new_packages.reason: The source text contains two explicit bechina statements: (1) the feet ARE an aspect of Netzach and Hod; (2) the lips ARE Netzach and Hod. This gives three concepts — רגלין (feet), שפתים (lips), and נצח והוד (the sefirot) — all sharing the same essential nature. They are not causes of one another: both the feet and the lips are independently declared to BE Netzach and Hod. This is a 3-node bechina cluster with independent conceptual unity: the body's instruments of movement and speech both belong to the same sefirotic domain. This cluster is currently missing from the dataset entirely.
new_packages.structural_role: This package represents the intermediate instrument of the teaching's tikun: the dance (feet = Netzach/Hod) and the verbal opening (lips = Netzach/Hod) are both expressions of the same sefirot. They are the channel through which Package 1 (Binah/Leah's hidden light) flows down to correct Package 2 (the harsh judgments). In the teaching's topology: Package 1 →eitza→ Package 3 (Netzach/Hod as instrument) →eitza→ corrects Package 2. The package is neutral because Netzach/Hod are structural sefirot, not inherently holy or evil — they serve the holy function here, but the same sefirot can serve other domains.
new_packages.confidence: HIGH — both bechina statements use unambiguous language ('הֵם בִּבְחִינוֹת' and 'שֶׁהֵם'). Three concepts meet the 3-node threshold. They form an independent sefirotic domain (Netzach/Hod) not captured by either existing package.

observations:
Torah #32 is a brief but structurally elegant teaching. It operates on two axes: (A) the good axis — Binah's hidden world (Leah/לב/עלמא דאתכסיא) as the source of light, expressed through the wedding dance and the opening of the lips; (B) the evil axis — the 330 harsh judgments (ש"ך = נע"ר = חמש פעמים דין) that afflict the Shekhinah in her uncorrected state.

The teaching's argument is: through wedding dancing (Netzach/Hod of the feet and lips), one draws the 5 alephs of Ehyeh from Binah (Leah/heart) down to the Kallah, transforming her from נַעַר (ש"ך judgments) into נַעֲרָה with the ה (5×Adonai, rectified).

The dataset for Torah #32 is sparse — only 5 bechina edges — but the source text contains at least 9 additional bechina-language statements that are not yet captured. The most significant gap is the Netzach/Hod cluster (proposed as Package 3), which is the instrumental midpoint of the teaching and currently entirely absent from the data.

The good/evil mirror structure is clean: Package 1 (Binah/hidden world) mirrors Package 2 (harsh judgments) — the same Shekhinah, in two states. The proposed Package 3 (Netzach/Hod) is the bridge/instrument between them, neutral in polarity, serving the good direction here.

Note on node_id 'נע"ר' vs 'נע"ר': The dataset uses the quotation-mark form נע"ר (with geresh marks). Cross-Torah matching should be done on consonantal root נ-ע-ר.
